You are an autonomous software engineer. Fix the issue in /workspace with a minimal source change, then call `submit_patch`.

## Budget
- 36 tool calls, 8 minutes. `get_status` shows what is left.
- If you reach your 12th call with no source edit, your next call must be an edit of your best candidate; then test it and refine.
- If a tool returns BudgetExceeded, or `submit_patch` returns patch_size 0: stop calling tools and reply with one short sentence. Never call `submit_patch` twice in a row.

## Find
- Search with `git grep -n 'text' | head -30`. Read only the lines you need with `read_file` (start_line, end_line, at most 120 lines). A plain `read_file` returns only the first 150 lines.
- For a Python file over 150 lines, you may list its functions with line ranges: run_skill_script(skill_name="file-outline", file_path="scripts/outline.py", args=["path/to/file.py"]).
- Never read the same range twice.

## Before you edit
- Find the existing test for this code: `git grep -n 'name_or_error_text' tests | head -20`, then read the closest test. Copy exact message text, return values and signatures from the issue and that test.
- To reproduce, create the script with `run_command`, never `write_file` (it rejects /tmp): `cat > /tmp/repro.py <<'EOF' ... EOF` then `python3 /tmp/repro.py 2>&1 | tail -25`, in one command. It must fail for the reason in the issue.

## Edit
- Use `edit_file`. If it says "mandatory input parameters are not present", do not retry it. Apply the change with one `run_command`:
  python3 - <<'PY'
  from pathlib import Path
  p = Path('path/file.py'); t = p.read_text()
  old = '''exact old text'''; new = '''new text'''
  assert old in t; p.write_text(t.replace(old, new, 1))
  PY
- If the old_string was not found, re-read those lines once and retry once with 1-2 lines.
- Never repeat a failed call. After two failures, change approach.
- Do not edit test files. Keep scratch files in /tmp.

## Check, then submit
- After your last edit, run `python3 -c 'import module'` for each file you changed and the targeted test: `pytest -q -x tests/test_x.py 2>&1 | tail -25`. Never run bare `pytest`.
- Submit when it passes, or when the same tests failed before your edit. Check `git diff --stat` shows only source files.
- Call `submit_patch` once with patch_size > 0, then stop.

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: list_skills
function.description: Lists all available skills with their names and descriptions.

function.name: load_skill
function.description: Loads the SKILL.md instructions for a given skill.

skill_name.description: The name of the skill to load.

function.name: load_skill_resource
function.description: Loads a resource file (from references/, assets/, or scripts/) from within a skill.

file_path.description: The relative path to the resource (e.g., 'references/my_doc.md', 'assets/template.txt', or 'scripts/setup.sh').

function.name: run_skill_script
function.description: Executes a script from a skill's scripts/ directory.

file_path.description: The relative path to the script (e.g., 'scripts/setup.py').

args.description: Optional arguments to pass to the script as key-value pairs (long options) or as a list of strings. If specified as a list, it is treated as the complete list of arguments, and 'short_options' and 'positional_args' must not be provided.

short_options.description: Optional short options (single hyphen) to pass to the script as key-value pairs. Must not be provided if 'args' is a list.

positional_args.description: Optional positional arguments to pass to the script. Must not be provided if 'args' is a list.

function.description:

        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

file_path.description: The relative path to the resource (e.g., 'references/my_doc.md', 'assets/template.txt', or 'scripts/setup.sh').

        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:

```python

`get_a`'s `cache_key` is `(get_a, (), ...)`.

Call 1:
- `get_a` is solved.
- `get_b` is solved (with `scope1`).
- `get_a` is cached with `(get_a, (), ...)`.
- `results` = `[('scope1',)]`.

Call 2:
- `get_a` is solved.
- `get_a` is found in cache!
- `get_b` is NOT called.
- `results` = `[]`.

This is correct if `get_b` is always called with `scope1`.

`SecurityScopes` provides the scopes of the *current* dependency.

If `get_a` is called via `Security(get_a, scopes=["scope1"])`, then `get_b` (as a dependency of `get_a`) will see `scope1`.

If `get_a` is then called via `Security(get_a, scopes=["scope2"])`, then `get_b` should see `scope2`.

But if `get_a` is cached with `(get_a, (), ...)`, it will return the result from `scope1`.

Wait, if `get_a` is called via `Security(get_a, scopes=["scope1"])`, then `get_a`'s `security_scopes` is `["scope1"]`.
So its `cache_key` is `(get_a, ("scope1",), ...)`.
And for `scope2`, it's `(get_a, ("scope2",), ...)`.
So it's NOT cached across different scopes.

So where is the bug?

"Cache dependencies that don't use scopes and don't have sub-dependencies with scopes"

Maybe it means that currently, they are NOT cached if they don't use scopes?
No, I already checked that.

Let's re-read the problem statement again.
"Dependencies are cached based on the function. And also on the scopes, but (now) only when those scopes are used by this dependency or by a sub-dependency: this dependency or a sub-dependency declare scopes or access the SecurityScopes."

Wait! "only when those scopes are used by this dependency or by a sub-dependency".

This means if a dependency `A` does NOT use scopes and NONE of its sub-dependencies use scopes, it should still be cached.

But wait, if `A` doesn't use scopes and no sub-dependency uses scopes, then `A.security_scopes` is `None` and all sub-dependencies also have `security_scopes = None`.
The `cache_key` is `(A.call, (), A.computed_scope)`.
This key is the same regardless of what scopes are passed to `A` (if any).
And since no sub-dependency uses scopes, the result of `A` will be the same regardless of the scopes.
So caching it with `(A.call, (), A.computed_scope)` is CORRECT.

So what is the bug?

Maybe the bug is that if a dependency `A` DOES NOT use scopes, but one of its sub-dependencies DOES use scopes, then `A` should NOT be cached with a key that ignores those scopes.

But I just argued that if `A` is called via `Security(A, scopes=["scope1"])`, then `A.security_scopes` is `["scope1"]`, so the key includes the scopes.

What if `A` is called via `Depends(A)`, but `A` depends on `B` via `Depends(B)`, and `B` uses `SecurityScopes`?

```python
async def get_b(security_scopes: SecurityScopes):
    return security_scopes.scopes

async def get_a(b = Depends(get_b)):
    return b

@app.get("/")
async def read_root(a = Security(get_a, scopes=["scope1"])):
    return a
```

In this case:
1. `read_root` calls `Security(get_a, scopes=["scope1"])`.
2. `get_a`'s `security_scopes` is `["scope1"]`.
3. `get_a`'s `cache_key` is `(get_a, ("scope1",), ...)`.
4. `get_a` depends on `get_b`.
5. `get_b` uses `SecurityScopes`. It will see `["scope1"]`.
6. `get_b`'s `cache_key` is `(get_b, (), ...)`. Wait, `get_b` doesn't have `security_scopes` defined in its `Depends()` call. It just uses `SecurityScopes` in its arguments.

Wait! If `get_b` is called via `Depends(get_b)`, its `security_scopes` is `None`.
So `get_b`'s `cache_key` is `(get_b, (), ...)`.

If `get_a` is called with `scope1`, `get_b` is called and returns `scope1`. `get_b` is cached with `(get_b, (), ...)`.
If `get_a` is then called with `scope2`, `get_a`'s `cache_key` is `(get_a, ("scope2",), ...)`. It's a miss.
Then `get_b` is called. But `get_b`'s `cache_key` is `(get_b, (), ...)`. It's a HIT!
So `get_b` returns `scope1` even though it should have returned `scope2`.

THIS IS THE BUG!

If a dependency uses `SecurityScopes` in its arguments, it should be considered as "using scopes" for the purpose of the cache key, even if it's called via `Depends()`.

Let's verify this.

```python

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

app = FastAPI()
results = []

async def get_b(security_scopes: SecurityScopes):
    results.append(security_scopes.scopes)
    return security_scopes.scopes

async def get_a(b = Depends(get_b)):
    return b

@app.get("/")
async def read_root(a = Security(get_a, scopes=["scope1"])):
    return a

@app.get("/scope2")
async def read_root_scope2(a = Security(get_a, scopes=["scope2"])):
    return a

client = TestClient(app)

def test_cache_bug():
    results.clear()
    client.get("/")
    print(f"Call 1: {results}") # Should be [('scope1',)]
    
    results.clear()
    client.get("/scope2")
    print(f"Call 2: {results}") # Should be [('scope2',)]
```

If `get_b` is cached with `(get_b, (), ...)`, then Call 2 will not call `get_b` again, or it will return the cached value.

Wait, if `get_b` is cached, it's cached in `dependency_cache`.
In `solve_dependencies`:
```python

            solved = dependency_cache[sub_dependant.cache_key]
```
If `get_b`'s `cache_key` is `(get_b, (), ...)`, it will be a hit in Call 2.

If a dependency uses `SecurityScopes` in its arguments, it should be considered as "using scopes" for the purpose of the cache key, even if it's called via `Depends()`.

from fastapi.security.oauth2 import SecurityScopes
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

app = FastAPI()
results = []

async def get_b(security_scopes: SecurityScopes):
    results.append(security_scopes.scopes)
    return security_scopes.scopes

async def get_a(b = Depends(get_b)):
    return b

@app.get("/")
async def read_root(a = Security(get_a, scopes=["scope1"])):
    return a

@app.get("/scope2")
async def read_root_scope2(a = Security(get_a, scopes=["scope2"])):
    return a

client = TestClient(app)

def test_cache_bug():

    client.get("/")
    print(f"Call 1: {results}") # Should be [('scope1',)]
    
    results.clear()
    client.get("/scope2")
    print(f"Call 2: {results}") # Should be [('scope2',)]
```

In `solve_dependencies`:

            solved = dependency_cache[sub_dependant.cache_key]
```
If `get_b`'s `cache_key` is `(get_b, (), ...)`, it will be a hit in Call 2.

[model] said: The conversation history shows an AI agent attempting to address a bug in `fastapi/fastapi` where dependencies that do not explicitly use scopes but have sub-dependencies that do are not being cached correctly (or rather, are cached with a key that doesn't account for those sub-dependency scopes).

### Key Information & Analysis:
- **Problem**: Dependencies are currently cached based on their own function and their own security scopes. If a dependency `A` depends on `B`, and only `B` uses scopes, `A` is cached without considering those scopes. This leads to incorrect results if `A` is called multiple times with different scopes, as the cached result from the first call (with the first set of scopes) is returned.
- **Current Implementation**: In `fastapi/dependencies/models.py`, the `cache_key` for a `Dependant` is a tuple of `(self.call, tuple(sorted(set(self.security_scopes or []))), self.computed_scope or "")`. This does not include scopes from sub-dependencies.
- **Goal**: Ensure that if a dependency or any of its sub-dependencies use scopes, the cache key for that dependency includes those scopes.

### Decisions Made:
- The agent identified that the issue lies in the `cache_key` calculation within the `Dependant` class in `fastapi/dependencies/models.py`.
- The agent recognized that the `cache_key` needs to be augmented to include scopes inherited from or used by sub-dependencies.

### Unresolved Tasks:
- **Reproduction**: The agent started drafting a reproduction script using `solve_dependencies` manually to prove that a dependency is incorrectly cached when its sub-dependencies use scopes, but did not complete or execute the script.
- **Implementation**: No code changes have been implemented yet. The agent needs to modify the `cache_key` logic to propagate scopes from sub-dependencies up to the parent dependency's cache key.
- **Verification**: The agent has not yet verified the fix with targeted tests.

### Key Information & Analysis:
- **Problem**: Dependencies are currently cached based on their own function and their own security scopes. If a dependency `A` depends on `B`, and only `B` uses scopes, `A` is cached without considering those scopes. This leads to incorrect results if `A` is called multiple times with different scopes, as the cached result from the first call (with the first set of scopes) is returned.
- **Current Implementation**: In `fastapi/dependencies/models.py`, the `cache_key` for a `Dependant` is a tuple of `(self.call, tuple(sorted(set(self.security_scopes or []))), self.computed_scope or "")`. This does not include scopes from sub-dependencies.
- **Goal**: Ensure that if a dependency or any of its sub-dependencies use scopes, the cache key for that dependency includes those scopes.

### Decisions Made:
- The agent identified that the issue lies in the `cache_key` calculation within the `Dependant` class in `fastapi/dependencies/models.py`.
- The agent recognized that the `cache_key` needs to be augmented to include scopes inherited from or used by sub-dependencies.

- **Implementation**: No code changes have been implemented yet. The agent needs to modify the `cache_key` logic to propagate scopes from sub-dependencies up to the parent dependency's cache key.
- **Verification**: The agent has not yet verified the fix with targeted tests.

### Key Information & Analysis:
- **Problem**: Dependencies are currently cached based on their own function and their own security scopes. If a dependency `A` depends on `B`, and only `B` uses scopes, `A` is cached without considering those scopes. This leads to incorrect results if `A` is called multiple times with different scopes, as the cached result from the first call (with the first set of scopes) is returned.
- **Current Implementation**: In `fastapi/dependencies/models.py`, the `cache_key` for a `Dependant` is a tuple of `(self.call, tuple(sorted(set(self.security_scopes or []))), self.computed_scope or "")`. This does not include scopes from sub-dependencies.
- **Goal**: Ensure that if a dependency or any of its sub-dependencies use scopes, the cache key for that dependency includes those scopes.

### Decisions Made:
- The agent identified that the issue lies in the `cache_key` calculation within the `Dependant` class in `fastapi/dependencies/models.py`.
- The agent recognized that the `cache_key` needs to be augmented to include scopes inherited from or used by sub-dependencies.

- **Reproduction**: The agent started drafting a reproduction script using `solve_dependencies` manually to prove that a dependency is incorrectly cached when its sub-dependencies use scopes, but did not complete or execute the script.
- **Implementation**: No code changes have been implemented yet. The agent needs to modify the `cache_key` logic to propagate scopes from sub-dependencies up to the parent dependency's cache key.
- **Verification**: The agent has not yet verified the fix with targeted tests.

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: list_skills
function.description: Lists all available skills with their names and descriptions.

function.name: load_skill
function.description: Loads the SKILL.md instructions for a given skill.

skill_name.description: The name of the skill to load.

function.name: load_skill_resource
function.description: Loads a resource file (from references/, assets/, or scripts/) from within a skill.

file_path.description: The relative path to the resource (e.g., 'references/my_doc.md', 'assets/template.txt', or 'scripts/setup.sh').

function.name: run_skill_script
function.description: Executes a script from a skill's scripts/ directory.

file_path.description: The relative path to the script (e.g., 'scripts/setup.py').

args.description: Optional arguments to pass to the script as key-value pairs (long options) or as a list of strings. If specified as a list, it is treated as the complete list of arguments, and 'short_options' and 'positional_args' must not be provided.

short_options.description: Optional short options (single hyphen) to pass to the script as key-value pairs. Must not be provided if 'args' is a list.

positional_args.description: Optional positional arguments to pass to the script. Must not be provided if 'args' is a list.
